config.goal: Port adam.cu (HeCBench adam-cuda; grid-stride Adam optimizer, 10 updates per parameter) to idiomatic SYCL 2020 with zero dpct helpers; the float32 parameters must match the C++ reference within atol 1e-5 + rtol 1e-4. Tolerance: 1 - 0.999^t cancels, so a 1-ulp difference in pow (GPU vs CPU libm) becomes a ~6e-5 relative difference in the bias-corrected v. Where v starts near 0 the update m/sqrt(v) is large and p moves by up to ~3 (min p is -2.02), so the error scales with |p|: simulating a 1-ulp pow change gives 3.15e-5 at that element and 8.5e-7 at the 99.99th percentile. The bound is then 6.7x above the worst case and over 10x above the rest, while an indexing, mode or update-order bug moves p by 1e-3 or more.

input.summary: Ported adam.cu to plain SYCL 2020 in migrated/adam.dp.cpp. The file has no dpct:: helpers, no DPCT_* macros and no #include <dpct/...>. It compiles with icpx -fsycl and add_dpct_include=false (0 errors, 0 warnings). Changes from the migrated version: dpct::pow became sycl::pow(b1, float(t)), matching the original powf(b1, t); the kernel is a 1-D grid-stride loop over sycl::nd_item<1> with the same update order and the same mode branch; the dpct::dim3 launch became sycl::nd_range<1> with a 256-wide work-group; buffers use sycl::malloc_device/sycl::free on an in-order queue; dev_ct1/q_ct1 and dpct_free were removed. Caveat: I have no run/verify tool, so the 1e-5 + 1e-4 tolerance check against the reference was not executed. The numerical argument rests on keeping the same float32 arithmetic and update order as the original. Remaining risk is the pow/sqrt implementations on the device versus host libm, which the task already accounts for.
